The '''B'omarr brain walker''' was a [[Spider/Legends|spider]]-like walker that allowed the disembodied [[Brain/Legends|brains]] of [[B'omarr Order/Legends|B'omarr monks]] to move around. Modified from the frame of a [[BT-16 perimeter droid]], the brain walkers were common sights around [[Jabba's Palace/Legends|Jabba's Palace]] on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]]. 

==Design==
[[File:BomarrBrainWalker-NEGTD.png|thumb|right|250px|A B'omarr brain walker]]
The basic frame of a B'omarr brain walker was a the modified frame of a [[BT-16 perimeter droid]]. [[B'omarr Order/Legends|B'omarr]] attendants assembled a series of armatures using parts from BT-16s. The modifications allowed<ref name="NEGTD" /> a shatterproof [[glassine]] jar<ref name="EGTD">''[[The Essential Guide to Droids]]''</ref> containing the [[Brain/Legends|brain]] of a B'omarr [[Monk/Legends|monk]] to be fitted to the frame, giving the monk a form of locomotion. As part of the modifications, the attendants removed the BT-16s [[Repeating blaster/Legends|repeating blaster]] and ventral [[Sensor/Legends|sensor]] globe to allow the installation of the jar.<ref name="NEGTD" /> 

The brain walkers underwent more modifications over the years, straying further from the BT-16's original design. By the time of the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], the units did not follow a single design pattern. Some units had four [[Durasteel/Legends|durasteel]] legs, while others were outfitted with up to nine limbs. Some units were fitted with [[Grasper arm/Legends|gripper claws]]. Most units included [[Speaker/Legends|speakers]] and [[Audio sensor/Legends|audio sensors]], allowing the monk to communicate. A row of colored lights was positioned at the base of the jar. During normal conditions, the lights glowed blue and green. If the lights were red, it indicated that the brain inside was "screaming" and not adjusting well to its new state. Each walker had a large storage abdomen, mounted at the read of the [[Servomotor/Legends|servomotor]] drive assembly that controlled the unit's legs. Retractable [[neurix tube]]s were located in the housing, and connected to the brain jar.<ref name="EGTD" />

Because of the marriage of mechanical components controlled by an organic [[Brain/Legends|brain]], B'omarr brain walkers met the minimum accepted standard for being defined as a "[[Cyborg/Legends|cyborg]]." Each walker had a [[Telepath response unit/Legends|telepath response unit]] installed to allow the brain, which was settled in a jar of [[nutrient fluid]], to control the armature.<ref name="NEGTD" />

==History==
{{Quote|A fanatical religious organization that believed they could achieve true enlightenment by having their brains surgically removed and placed into spider droid bodies.|[[Mayor/Legends|Mayor]] [[Mikdanyell Guh'rantt]], about the [[B'omarr Order/Legends|B'omarr Monks]].|<ref name="SWG:MMG">{{SWGcite|exp=RotW|type=conversation|Mayor Mikdanyell Guh'rantt|Tatooine}}</ref>}}
[[File:BomarrBrainWalkerModel.jpg|thumb|left|250px|A B'omarr brain walker]]
The B'omarr attendants faithfully maintained the armatures. When one of the monks had business to attend to, it [[Telepathy/Legends|telepathically]] summoned one of the walkers. The armature then picked up the brain jar and affixed it to the unit. An acolyte usually assisted with the procedure.<ref name="EGTD" />

One of the modified B'omarr version, seemingly without a brain, was present on [[Jib Kopatha]]'s home, [[Void Station]], in [[0 ABY/Legends|0 ABY]].<ref name="Empire19">[[Empire 19|''Empire'' 19]]</ref> The B'omarr in [[Jabba's Palace/Legends|Jabba's Palace]] were eager to initiate others into their way of life. Following [[Jabba Desilijic Tiure/Legends|Jabba]] the [[Hutt/Legends|Hutt's]] [[Death/Legends|death]] at the [[Battle of the Great Pit of Carkoon]], the monks forcibly removed some of the brains of Jabba's henchmen, including [[Bib Fortuna/Legends|Bib Fortuna]].<ref name="EGTD" />
